item.title: Agency in the Age of AI
item.content:encoded:
Paul Leonardi, :?

Alex Murray, :?

Frank Nagle, :?

Nelson Phillips, :?

Juliana Schroeder, :?

Paula Ungureanu, :?

Elisa Villani, :?

The fundamental concept of agency—who can act, what action requires, and who bears responsibility—has long shaped organizational theory. With intelligent technologies now actively participating in organizational processes, this foundational understanding is being challenged as action, intention, and consequences can no longer be attributed solely to individual human actors.

This special issue invites theoretically sophisticated research that reimagines agency when humans and machines co-produce organizational action. The editors seek work that both reconceptualizes agency itself and examines how this shift transforms core organizational phenomena including behavior, leadership, careers, strategy, institutions, and governance.

Appel publié par Organization Science. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Reconceptualization of agency in contexts involving artificial intelligence and human actors
  • Distribution and location of agency when action is co-produced by people and machines
  • Implications for organizational behavior and motivation theories
  • Leadership and decision-making in AI-augmented environments
  • Control mechanisms and accountability in human-AI systems
  • Value creation involving intelligent technologies
  • Career development and work structures affected by AI participation
  • Institutional change driven by agentic AI
  • Technological change and organizational adaptation
  • Management and organizational control with autonomous systems
  • Strategic implications of distributed agency
  • Entrepreneurship in the age of AI
  • Sociology of work and labor transformation
  • Information systems and autonomous action
  • Governance frameworks for AI-driven organizational action

Timeline

  • February 1, 2027: Submissions due

item.title: AI-Enabled Frontiers in Organizational Science
item.content:encoded:
Claudine Gartenberg, .pop

Sharique Hasan, .pop

Lamar Pierce, .pop

Christopher Bail, .pop

Hengchen Dai, .pop

Oliver Hauser, .pop

Hatim Rahman, .pop

Dennis Zhang, .pop

This special issue asks a fundamental question about artificial intelligence and social science: do we want it to produce faster, cheaper versions of what we already do, or do we want fundamentally new science? Returning to Organization Science's founding mission—Daft and Lewin's 1990 call to break out of the "normal science straitjacket" and March's "exploration of new possibilities"—we want to shift our focus to how AI is changing the production of science and how it can expand our knowledge, rather than merely increasing the number of papers through efficiency and reduced labor.

In this call for science, we seek contributions that reimagine what a social science research contribution is in an AI-enabled world, encouraging wild ideas and radical innovation over obvious incremental improvement. We are not looking for conventional full-length papers with AI-related content, nor "AI slop"—we want the innovative applications themselves.

Appel publié par Organization Science. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-enabled research loops under human direction
  • Reusable research infrastructure
  • New forms of measurement
  • AI-enabled qualitative and theory-building work
  • Synthetic social systems
  • New approaches to established research designs
  • Critical or boundary-setting work on the limits of AI-enabled science
  • Reimagining social science research contributions in an AI-enabled world

Timeline
